title: Inject FakeLocalDayClock into TrackCreationService's B3 back-date tests instead of reading the wall clock

evidence.quote: expect(daysBack, 5, reason: 'offset:5 must be exactly 5 days in the past');

why: Neither B3 test overrides LocalDayClock, so DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() reads the real system clock both for the test's 'before' and again inside the SUT's _parseProgramStartingRef moments later. Duration.inDays truncates: (Duration(days:5) - Duration(microseconds:1)).inDays == 4, verified directly in this Dart VM; an empirical 200k-iteration back-to-back DateTime.now() sample in this same environment showed roughly 4% of pairs returning a non-zero gap (up to 70us), meaning daysBack can legitimately compute to 4 instead of 5 and fail expect(daysBack, 5, ...) for reasons unrelated to any real regression. This is exactly the flakiness class LocalDayClock/FakeLocalDayClock exists to eliminate, and the sibling provision_track_use_case_test.dart correctly uses FakeLocalDayClock for the equivalent B3 assertions — this file is the outlier.
recommendation: Thread a FakeLocalDayClock(seed) into TrackCreationService/_parseProgramStartingRef so the test's 'before' and the SUT's 'now' are the identical fixed instant, making daysBack deterministic.
acceptance_criteria: Test passes across many repeated runs with an artificial delay inserted between test setup and SUT invocation
Test no longer depends on two independent real-clock reads landing in the same tick
